chunks: Ismaʿīl ibn Muslim narrated from al-Ṣādiq Jaʿfar ibn Muḥammad, from his father عليه السلام, that he said:
Testimony is invalidated in cases of usury and janaf. If the witnesses say, "We do not know," then let them go; but if they knew, then discipline them with taʿzīr.

key_terms.الرِّبَا: usury or unlawful increase in financial dealings
key_terms.الْجَنَفِ: deviation, bias, or wrongful inclining from justice
key_terms.سَبِيلَهُمْ: their way, meaning they are to be released
key_terms.عَزِّرْهُمْ: discipline them with ta'zir, a discretionary punishment

ai.seo_question: When is testimony invalidated, and what is done with witnesses who falsely claim ignorance?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning the invalidation of testimony in matters involving riba and janaf. It also states that witnesses claiming ignorance are to be released, but if their knowledge is established, they are to be subjected to ta'zir.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.3348 - It is narrated by Isma'il ibn Muslim from Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq (as) from his father Imam Muhammad ibn Ali Al-Baqir (as) that he said:

"Testimonies are invalidated in cases of usury (riba) and bias (janaf). If the witnesses say, 'We do not know,' then release them. However, if they are found to have known, then they should be disciplined (ta'zir)."
